passage:
seminar — 研讨会
Last Thursday, the university's Media and Evidence Society held a seminar titled 'Productivity Claims: Who Says So?' About forty students attended.

survey — 调查
The blog's readers were mostly people who already liked short sessions, so the survey could not speak for all workers.

respondents — 受访者
The first speaker, Marco Li, presented a claim from a popular blog: 'Working in short bursts makes everyone more productive.' Marco reported that the blog had surveyed its readers and that most respondents said they preferred short work sessions.

agenda — 议程
Her team had observed twelve meetings in one department and found that three of them had no clear agenda and no written decisions.

cautioned — 提醒；警告
Priya cautioned that twelve meetings in one department cannot represent most workplaces.

volunteers — 志愿者
The third speaker, Tom Becker, examined a claim about tools: 'Most productivity apps improve focus.' He described a small trial in which twenty volunteers used a timer app for two weeks.

quantifier — 限定词（表示数量范围的词）
Each student rewrote one claim using a more careful verb and a narrower quantifier.

indicated — 表明；显示
Marco changed his sentence to 'The blog reported that some readers preferred short sessions.' Priya wrote 'The observation suggested that some meetings in one department lacked clear agendas.' Tom wrote 'The trial indicated that some volunteers felt more focused.' Dr.
